en.title: 8 Games If You Loved 007: First Light
en.summary: Still craving that blend of stealth, action, and gadgets after playing 007: First Light? This list dives into titles that capture that same espionage thrill and high-octane gameplay.
en.body:
## 1. Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain
This open-world stealth-action masterpiece from Konami (2015) lets you infiltrate enemy bases with unparalleled freedom, utilizing a vast arsenal of gadgets and tactical approaches. Its deep gameplay systems and mature narrative echo the strategic espionage found in Bond titles, offering a similarly rewarding experience.

## 2. Hitman (2016)
IO Interactive's rebooted Hitman franchise excels at putting players in the shoes of Agent 47, a master assassin who relies on disguises, environmental manipulation, and precise execution. If you enjoyed the strategic takedowns and gadget use in 007: First Light, Hitman's sandbox levels provide endless replayability for creative kills.

## 3. Splinter Cell: Blacklist
As Sam Fisher, you'll once again be tasked with covert operations in this 2013 Ubisoft title. Blacklist masterfully blends stealth and action, allowing players to choose between ghost-like infiltration or a more direct, combat-heavy approach, much like the adaptable gameplay in 007: First Light.

## 4. Uncharted 4: A Thief's End
While more focused on cinematic action and platforming, Naughty Dog's 2016 conclusion to Nathan Drake's story features plenty of gunplay, puzzle-solving, and globe-trotting adventure reminiscent of a Bond film. The set pieces and character interactions capture that larger-than-life entertainment factor.

## 5. Deus Ex: Mankind Divided
This 2016 Eidos-Montréal title offers a rich cyberpunk world where player choice dictates the approach to missions. Combining stealth, combat, and a heavy emphasis on augmentations that function like advanced gadgets, it provides a deep, immersive experience for those who enjoy tactical infiltration.

## 6. The Getaway
This gritty 2002 PlayStation 2 title from Team Soho thrust players into the criminal underworld of London. Its focus on driving, shooting, and a compelling narrative gave it a distinct cinematic feel that aligns with the stylish action often associated with the Bond universe.

## 7. Syphon Filter: Dark Mirror
Originally released on PSP in 2004, this installment in the Syphon Filter series puts players in control of Gabe Logan, a secret agent using advanced weaponry and gadgets to thwart global threats. Its blend of third-person shooting and stealth mechanics offers a solid espionage experience.

## 8. Alpha Protocol
Developed by Obsidian Entertainment and released in 2010, Alpha Protocol is an RPG that puts you in the role of a secret agent. It allows for significant player choice in dialogue and mission approach, offering a unique take on the spy genre with consequences for your actions.

Bottom Line: These games offer a diverse range of spy-infused adventures, from tactical stealth to explosive action, ensuring your espionage itch is scratched long after the credits roll.
